questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The reputation of german academic rigour, as well as learning german.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In general the stay i Münich was great. I learnt a lot of german, and learnt alot at the university. A negative is the amount of bureaucracy, especially for the Erasmus-grant. The amount of work and time used to get this grant is daunting, and a lot more than other grants.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: In general, it was pretty easy. Although more specialized information about how my specific department (Allgemeine und Vergleichende Literaturwissenschaft), was kinda difficult.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university had a introductory seminar on zoom.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy through the Erasmus-incomming team at my host university. Though it is only easy if you have money for the expensive Münich rent.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Rent is expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Course registration was not too big a problem. Exam registration was a different story. It was very much up to the teacher of the courses.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was a course-catalog online. Here i could see the e-mails of the professors teaching the course. As i was an Erasmus-student, i had to write to all the professors, and they all answered me, and registered me for the courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had a so-called LMU-buddy. She helped me a lot with practical stuff. Also there was a Erasmus office which were helpfull.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Completely succesfull. I registered for all the courses i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of bureaucracy, but fortunately there are often a person you can call and ask for help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses varied a lot. Most courses were very high level, with a large curriculum of difficult texts. Fewer courses were easier, and a single course was on the edge of being too easy, with a small curriculum and had very introductory content.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The courses at LMU (host) had fewer students, which allowed for a more free discussion in class, and more attention from the professor regarding exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1) Hauptseminar, 13629: Musik und/als Sprache: Thomas Mann, Doktor Faustus 
2) Lektürekurs, 13435: Weltliteratur: Rainer Maria Rilke: Die Aufzeichnungen des Malte Laurids Brigge 
3) Lektürekurs, 13431: Weltliteratur: Everyday heroes. James Joyces Ulysses
4) Seminar, 13622: The Rhetoric of Pain in Nineteenth-Century Abolitionism
5) Seminar, 13624: Prometheus gegen Thersites: Der Dichter zwischen Genieästhetik und Literatursoziologie
6) Blockseminar, 13620: Borges: Gedichte und Erzählungen

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The courses on Thomas Mann, Rainar Maria Rilke and 'Prometheus gegen Thersites' were all very high level and interesting courses. The texts were closely read, and the professors really showed why these texts are classics.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are many (high)cultural opportunities i Münich.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Concerts, parties, sports. Quite many things.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the opera.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the Alps.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. THe language barrier was the toughest one to crack.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language was by far the most challenging. But german culture is not so different from danish.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The high-culture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Have good german language skills. By far the most important aspect.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go do it! It is an amazing place.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning the language and the german academic culture. Reading Kant and Thomas Mann.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language.
